metadata.description: Comprehensive information about mythical and fictional horses from various cultures and media

greek_roman.name: Pegasus
greek_roman.description: Immortal winged horse born from the blood of Medusa
powers: Creation of springs by stomping hoof
greek_roman.symbolism: Divine inspiration, poetic imagination, transition between earth and heaven
famous_stories: Becoming a constellation by Zeus's command

greek_roman.name: Horses of Helios
greek_roman.description: Fire-breathing horses that pulled the sun chariot across the sky
famous_stories: Phaethon's disastrous attempt to drive the sun chariot

greek_roman.name: Arion
greek_roman.description: Extremely swift immortal horse with a black mane and tail
greek_roman.parentage: Poseidon and Demeter (both in horse form)

greek_roman.name: Xanthus and Balius
greek_roman.description: Immortal horses given to Peleus as a wedding gift

details.name: Hrímfaxi
details.description: Brings night by sprinkling dew from mane

celtic.name: Enbarr
celtic.description: Magical horse from the Celtic Otherworld who could travel over water

celtic.name: Kelpie
celtic.description: Shapeshifting water spirit that often appears as a horse
celtic.behavior: Lures humans to ride it, then drowns them
celtic.appearance: Usually black, with a constantly dripping mane

celtic.name: Each Uisge
celtic.description: Dangerous water horse spirit similar to kelpie but dwelling in seas and lochs
celtic.behavior: More dangerous than kelpie, completely devours victims except liver

eastern.name: Tianma
eastern.associated_with: Emperor Wu of Han and celestial realms
eastern.appearance: Often depicted with dragon-like features, wings, or fiery manes

eastern.name: Buraq
eastern.description: Divine steed that carried Prophet Muhammad
eastern.associated_with: Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj) of Muhammad
eastern.appearance: White horse-like creature with wings and human face
powers: Flight at the speed of light

eastern.name: Kanthaka
eastern.significance: Carried Prince Siddhartha on his departure from palace life
eastern.fate: Died of grief after Siddhartha left to become an ascetic

other_cultures.name: Chollima
other_cultures.description: Mythical winged horse that could cover great distances
other_cultures.speed: Said to travel 1,000 li (400 km) in a day

other_cultures.name: Tulpar
other_cultures.appearance: Present on Tatar, Kazakh, and Kyrgyz emblems

other_cultures.name: Al-Borak
other_cultures.description: Divine horse with human face and peacock tail

centaurs.description: Creatures with upper body of human and lower body of horse

notable_examples.name: Chiron
notable_examples.description: Wise centaur known for teaching heroes

notable_examples.name: Nessus
notable_examples.description: Centaur whose blood ultimately killed Heracles
notable_examples.story: After being shot by Heracles, gave poisoned blood to Deianeira as false love potion

notable_examples.name: Pholus
notable_examples.fate: Accidentally killed by one of Heracles' poisoned arrows

centaurs.behavior: Most were wild and uncivilized, representing untamed nature and base desires
centaurs.exceptions: Chiron and few others represented wisdom and civilized teaching

hippogriff.description: Creature with front half of an eagle and hind half of a horse
hippogriff.origin: Greco-Roman mythology, popularized in Renaissance literature
hippogriff.symbolism: Impossibility (as griffins and horses were natural enemies)
hippogriff.famous_examples: Hippogriff in Orlando Furioso by Ludovico Ariosto

hippocampus.description: Marine creature with upper body of horse and lower body of fish
hippocampus.appearance: Horse's head and forelegs with fish tail or sea serpent body

unicorn.description: Horse-like creature with single spiral horn on forehead
unicorn.origin: Multiple ancient cultures, evolved in European medieval lore
unicorn.historical_context: Possibly based on misidentified rhinos or other animals
symbolism: Healing (horn could purify water and heal sickness)

appearance.medieval: Goat-like beard, lion's tail, cloven hooves
appearance.modern: More horse-like, with single horn and sometimes cloven hooves

cultural_significance.heraldry: Symbol of Scotland, featured in British royal coat of arms
cultural_significance.modern: Symbol of fantasy, innocence, and magic in popular culture

kirin.description: Chinese mythical creature with dragon head, scales, and horse-like body
kirin.origin: Chinese mythology (qilin), adapted in Japanese as kirin

appearance.chinese: Dragon scales, ox hooves, deer body, horse-like shape, single horn

powers: Walking on grass without bending it

literature.name: Black Beauty
literature.description: Gentle black stallion who narrates his life story
literature.significance: One of first animal perspective novels, advocated for humane treatment

literature.name: Shadowfax
literature.source: The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien
literature.description: Lord of all horses, steed of Gandalf
literature.appearance: Silver-gray, no bridle or saddle needed

literature.name: Bucephalus
literature.source: Historical/semi-legendary horse of Alexander the Great
literature.description: Massive black stallion with a white star
literature.legend: Untamable until young Alexander noticed it was afraid of its shadow
literature.historical_significance: Accompanied Alexander through conquests, city named after him

literature.name: Rocinante
literature.source: Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes
literature.description: Thin, past-his-prime horse of Don Quixote
literature.symbolism: Parallels his master's delusional grandeur vs. reality
literature.name_meaning: Previously a workhorse (rocín) but now elevated 'ante' (before)

film_television.name: Secretariat
film_television.source: Historical racehorse featured in 2010 Disney film
film_television.achievements: Triple Crown winner in 1973, set records still standing today
film_television.significance: One of greatest racehorses in history
film_television.appearance: Chestnut with three white socks and a star

film_television.name: Artax
film_television.famous_scene: Tragic death in the Swamp of Sadness
film_television.symbolism: Loss of hope and deep grief

film_television.name: Spirit
film_television.source: Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron (2002 film)
film_television.appearance: Buckskin mustang with black mane and tail

animation_comics.name: Rainbow Dash
animation_comics.source: My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic
animation_comics.description: Pegasus pony with rainbow mane and tail

animation_comics.name: Rapidash
animation_comics.description: Fire-type Pokémon resembling a unicorn with flames
animation_comics.appearance: White horse with horn and mane/tail of flames

animation_comics.name: Epona
animation_comics.source: The Legend of Zelda video game series
animation_comics.special_traits: Comes when called with special song
animation_comics.appearance: Chestnut with white mane and blaze

folklore_fairytales.name: Swift-Wind
folklore_fairytales.description: Magical horse that can travel vast distances instantly
folklore_fairytales.variations: Similar horses appear in Russian, Eastern European tales

folklore_fairytales.name: Falada
folklore_fairytales.source: The Goose Girl (Brothers Grimm fairy tale)
folklore_fairytales.description: Talking horse who continues to speak even after death
folklore_fairytales.story: Helps expose the false princess after being beheaded
folklore_fairytales.significance: Symbol of truth that cannot be silenced

death_horses.name: Pale Horse of Death
death_horses.description: Mount of the Fourth Horseman of the Apocalypse
death_horses.quote: And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death

death_horses.name: Sleipnir as Psychopomp
death_horses.description: Odin's horse that could travel to underworld

death_horses.name: Night Mare
death_horses.description: Malevolent spirit or demon in horse form
death_horses.folklore: Believed to sit on chests of sleepers, causing bad dreams

divine_horses.name: Sun Horses
divine_horses.description: Horses pulling sun chariots across the sky

fertility_prosperity.name: Mari Lwyd
fertility_prosperity.description: Horse skull on pole carried door-to-door
fertility_prosperity.ritual: Carried at New Year with songs and challenges

horse_constellations.name: Pegasus
horse_constellations.description: One of largest constellations in northern sky
notable_features: 51 Pegasi (first sun-like star found with exoplanet)

horse_constellations.name: Equuleus
horse_constellations.mythology: Various associations including foal of Castor, brother of Pegasus

horse_constellations.name: Centaurus
notable_features: Alpha Centauri (closest star system to Sun)
Omega Centauri (largest globular cluster in Milky Way)
